paragraphs: Greedy Coordinate Gradient, or GCG, searches for adversarial prompt suffixes that can cause a language model to break its safety behavior. It is effective but expensive to optimize, which limits how extensively researchers can use it to study model safety. This paper introduces probe sampling to reduce that computational cost.

The method uses a smaller draft model to help screen candidate prompts. Its central step is to dynamically assess how closely the draft model's predictions agree with those of the target model. When agreement is strong, the draft model filters out many candidates, reducing the computation required from the target. The reliance on the smaller model therefore depends on measured similarity.

On AdvBench with Llama2-7b-chat, the authors report speedups of up to 5.6 times while maintaining or improving attack success rates. They also report accelerations of 1.8 times for AutoPrompt and 2.4 times for both APE and AutoDAN. These results suggest that adaptive candidate screening can benefit several forms of prompt optimization, beyond GCG alone.
neurips-2024-accelerating-greedy-coordin.tldr: Probe sampling adaptively uses a smaller model to screen prompt candidates, accelerating GCG and other prompt optimization methods.

paragraphs: Cloud cover makes satellite images harder to use in downstream applications. Progress on removing it also depends on having enough varied training examples and a common way to evaluate methods. AllClear addresses these needs with a public dataset containing four million images across 23,742 regions distributed around the world and covering diverse land uses.

Each region includes temporal observations throughout 2022. The collection brings together multispectral optical images from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9, radar images from Sentinel-1, and supporting products such as cloud masks and land cover maps. This combination makes it possible to study cloud removal using observations across time and different imaging modalities within one dataset.

The authors benchmark performance and report that increasing training data by a factor of 30 raises PSNR from 28.47 to 33.87. This provides empirical evidence that additional data improves reconstruction quality in their evaluation. They also investigate temporal coverage and the contributions of individual modalities through ablation studies, making AllClear a resource for examining which information helps cloud removal.
neurips-2024-allclear-a-comprehensive-da.tldr: AllClear supplies four million satellite images and a benchmark for studying how data scale, time coverage, and imaging modalities improve cloud removal.

paragraphs: Autoformalization translates mathematical statements written in ordinary language into a formal language. Language models can produce promising translations, but their first attempt is considerably less reliable than obtaining a correct result somewhere among several attempts. This paper targets that selection problem: given multiple candidate formalizations, how can a system choose the best one?

The proposed framework combines two kinds of consistency. Symbolic equivalence uses automated theorem provers to identify candidates that express the same logical content. Semantic consistency translates a candidate back into informal language and compares its text embedding with that of the original statement. These checks examine complementary relationships: agreement between formal candidates and preservation of the source statement's meaning.

Experiments on MATH and miniF2F show significant accuracy improvements across several language models and baseline methods. The contribution is a way to make better use of a model's collection of proposed answers through scoring and selection. Logical agreement alone and similarity to the original wording provide different evidence, and the framework uses both to guide its choice.
neurips-2024-autoformalize-mathematical-.tldr: The framework selects mathematical formalizations by combining theorem-prover checks of logical agreement with checks that the original meaning is preserved.

paragraphs: Dataset distillation creates condensed representations of large image collections so that models can train more efficiently. This paper focuses on redundancy in the colors of distilled images. Its premise is that a compact training collection can use its color information more effectively by reducing repetition both within individual images and across the collection.

For individual images, the authors introduce a palette network that assigns pixels colors from a reduced color space. The assignments are adaptive: regions identified as important for model training receive more distinct colors. At the dataset level, a separate initialization strategy selects representative images whose color patterns repeat less, using information gain to guide that selection.

The two components address different sources of wasted capacity. One distributes color detail within synthetic examples, while the other reduces overlap among the examples used to initialize distillation. Evaluations across multiple datasets and scenarios report better performance than existing distillation methods. The findings support treating color allocation and color diversity as explicit parts of the distillation process.
neurips-2024-color-oriented-redundancy-r.tldr: Color-aware dataset distillation reduces redundant colors within images and repeated color patterns across images to improve condensed training data.

paragraphs: This paper models how a learner can discover a rule expressed in natural language by conducting experiments. The challenge involves both revising beliefs after observing results and choosing which experiment to perform next. The proposed system connects language models with probabilistic inference so that these two activities can inform each other throughout learning.

Language models work alongside Monte Carlo algorithms that support inference over possible rules. The system updates its beliefs as evidence arrives and chooses experiments using information-theoretic criteria. In a comparison with human behavior on a Zendo-style task, approximately Bayesian belief updating alone is insufficient to account for the observations: allowing fuzzy, probabilistic rules is also a critical ingredient.

The authors additionally compare their method with recent approaches that use language models to generate and revise hypotheses. Their online inference method recovers the underlying rule more accurately and better supports optimal experiment design. Together, the findings connect successful rule discovery with uncertainty over hypotheses and suggest that a model of human performance should accommodate rules that are not strictly all-or-nothing.
neurips-2024-doing-experiments-and-revis.tldr: Combining language models with probabilistic inference improves experimental rule discovery and helps explain human behavior when fuzzy rules are included.

paragraphs: The paper studies a platform that repeatedly sets service fees to maximize revenue while learning demand. It observes transaction quantities and equilibrium prices shaped by both buyers and sellers. This creates two complications: ordinary least squares produces biased, inconsistent demand estimates, and forward-looking buyers may strategically misrepresent their preferences to improve their own outcomes.

The proposed algorithms combine deliberate random variation, instrumental-variable estimation, and a pricing design with low switching costs. The platform's actions serve as instruments for consistently estimating demand, even though those actions are not independent and identically distributed. The low-switching design encourages nearly truthful buyer behavior, while randomness helps balance gathering information with earning revenue.

The authors prove an expected regret bound, ignoring logarithmic factors, given by the smaller of the square root of the time horizon and the inverse square of supply randomness. They show this dependence is optimal up to logarithmic factors. The result identifies a change between performance regimes: randomness already present in supply can facilitate exploration and alter how the revenue shortfall scales.
neurips-2024-dynamic-service-fee-pricing.tldr: The paper develops provably efficient service-fee policies that learn demand through pricing actions while accounting for strategic buyers and supply randomness.

paragraphs: Exposure correction aims to restore images that are too bright or too dark. ECMamba addresses this task by combining Mamba-style sequence modeling with Retinex guidance, which separates reflectance and illumination information. The authors focus on integrating that separation into the architecture while also addressing the balance between correction quality and computational efficiency.

A trained Retinex estimator first maps an input into two intermediate representations that approximate the desired reflectance and illumination maps. Separate pathways then refine these representations through Exposure Correction Mamba Modules. This gives the restoration process distinct representations to work on, with each pathway dedicated to one part of the Retinex decomposition.

At the center of those modules is Retinex-SS2D, a selective state-space layer guided by Retinex information. It uses a two-dimensional scanning strategy based on deformable feature aggregation to improve efficiency and effectiveness. Experiments and ablation studies support the performance of the overall system and the importance of its components. The contribution is therefore both a guided restoration architecture and a specialized operator for processing its image features.
neurips-2024-ecmamba-consolidating-selec.tldr: ECMamba combines separate reflectance and illumination restoration pathways with Retinex-guided state-space processing for efficient exposure correction.

paragraphs: ERBench turns relational databases into benchmarks for evaluating language-model answers and their accompanying rationales. Its central idea is to use the constraints built into a database as a source of automatically checkable structure. This supports questions whose complexity can grow while retaining ways to inspect intermediate answers.

Two types of constraint do different jobs. Functional dependencies identify critical keywords a model should know when a question specifies particular attribute values. Foreign keys connect records across tables, allowing questions to follow multiple linked steps. Those connections support arbitrarily long multi-hop questions and make it possible to locate errors along the sequence of intermediate answers.

The authors construct benchmarks from databases in several domains and compare contemporary language models. Their rationale checks look for the appropriate keywords, adding a verifiable signal beyond whether the final answer is correct. ERBench also supports changing databases, multimodal questions, and different prompting techniques. Its value lies in reusing structured knowledge and database constraints to produce evaluations that can evolve with their underlying data.
neurips-2024-erbench-an-entity-relations.tldr: ERBench uses relational database constraints to generate complex questions and automatically check answers and keywords in their rationales.

paragraphs: This paper asks how to store a collection of points using few bits while preserving enough information to estimate distances between them. The authors construct random nonlinear maps that produce compact sketches. With high probability, the sketches allow squared distances to be reported within a specified multiplicative error of one plus or minus epsilon.

The maps are built by repeatedly composing a particular random feature transformation. Each output coordinate takes one of two scaled values, so the result already has a binary representation. This distinguishes the construction from the usual Johnson–Lindenstrauss approach based on random linear maps, whose outputs need an additional conversion into bits before they become a digital sketch.

The direct binary output is a practical advantage of the construction, and the authors establish that it also uses fewer storage bits for some parameter ranges. That storage benefit is explicitly conditional rather than universal. Experiments, including nearest-neighbor search, validate the method and connect its distance-preservation properties with a task that depends on identifying nearby points.
neurips-2024-euclidean-distance-compress.tldr: Repeated random nonlinear mappings produce binary sketches that preserve approximate squared distances and can reduce storage for some parameter ranges.

paragraphs: People can recognize actions from very sparse motion cues, including point-light displays. The paper studies why this kind of biological motion perception remains difficult for AI models to generalize to. Its proposed Motion Perceiver uses only optical flow from local video patches, making motion patterns the input from which it predicts actions.

During training, the model learns representative flow snapshots through a competitive binding mechanism. It then integrates invariant motion representations to classify the action in a video. The authors evaluate generalization using 62,656 video stimuli across 24 biological-motion conditions, drawing on point-light displays used in neuroscience and comparisons with human observers.

Motion Perceiver outperforms the other AI models evaluated on these conditions, with a maximum reported improvement of 29% in top-1 action recognition accuracy. It also performs better on point-light versions of two standard video datasets. Psychophysics experiments reveal behavior aligned with human recognition of biological movement. These findings support the proposed motion representation as a route toward better generalization under sparse visual cues.
neurips-2024-flow-snapshot-neurons-in-ac.tldr: Motion Perceiver learns from local optical flow to improve action recognition in point-light displays and exhibits recognition behavior aligned with humans.

paragraphs: G3 estimates the geographic coordinates of a photograph taken anywhere in the world. The task is difficult because distant places can look similar and available image data is unevenly distributed geographically. The framework combines retrieval with generation to address both the interpretation of location clues and differences in retrieval quality across places.

Its first stage, Geo-alignment, jointly learns representations of images, GPS coordinates, and textual descriptions. These representations support retrieving images near the query's location. Geo-diversification then uses an ensemble of prompts to remain robust when retrieval works inconsistently across queries. Finally, Geo-verification combines GPS candidates obtained through retrieval and generation to make the location prediction.

The stages connect representation learning, prompting, and candidate verification within one process. This matters because the system is designed to handle variation in how useful retrieved examples are for different queries. Experiments on IM2GPS3k and YFCC4k report better performance than other state-of-the-art methods, supporting the effectiveness of the combined framework on those two benchmarks.
neurips-2024-g3-an-effective-and-adaptiv.tldr: G3 combines multimodal geographic alignment, prompt ensembles, and verification of retrieved and generated coordinates to improve worldwide photo geolocation.

paragraphs: Spatial transcriptomics measures molecular composition within tissue, while histology images reveal tissue structure. HEST-1k brings these sources together in a collection of 1,229 spatial transcriptomic profiles, each paired with a stained whole-slide image and extensive metadata. The project addresses a field where costs, changing technology, and limited standards have constrained computational work to small cohorts and narrow tasks.

The collection combines 153 public and internal cohorts covering 26 organs in humans and mice. It includes 367 cancer samples representing 25 cancer types. Processing the data identifies 2.1 million pairs linking gene expression with tissue morphology and more than 76 million nuclei, providing substantial material for examining relationships between molecular measurements and visible structure.

The authors also introduce HEST-Library, a Python package for working with these samples. They demonstrate the resources through pathology foundation-model benchmarking, biomarker exploration, and multimodal representation learning. HEST-Benchmark supplies the benchmarking use case. Together, the dataset, software, and benchmark create a shared basis for studying tissue appearance alongside spatial molecular information.
neurips-2024-hest-1k-a-dataset-for-spati.tldr: HEST-1k pairs spatial molecular profiles with tissue images and provides tools for pathology benchmarking, biomarker exploration, and multimodal learning.

paragraphs: HourVideo evaluates whether multimodal models can understand videos that extend over substantial periods of time. It contains 500 manually curated first-person videos from Ego4D, lasting between 20 and 120 minutes. The benchmark pairs these recordings with 12,976 multiple-choice questions, each offering five possible answers.

The questions cover a broad set of abilities: summarization, recalling events, tracking, and reasoning about space, time, causes, predictions, and counterfactual situations. Navigation questions involve moving between rooms and retrieving objects. This task range examines several ways of understanding an extended recording, connecting remembered visual information with reasoning about events and the environment.

The reported results show a large gap between model and human performance. Models including GPT-4 and LLaVA-NeXT improve only marginally over chance, while human experts achieve 85.0% compared with Gemini Pro 1.5's 37.3%. These findings make the benchmark a demanding test of long-video understanding. The authors also provide evaluation tools, prompts, and documentation to support its use.
neurips-2024-hourvideo-1-hour-video-lang.tldr: HourVideo tests understanding of long first-person videos and reveals a substantial performance gap between evaluated multimodal models and human experts.

paragraphs: PAC-Bayes theory can assess generalization and guide learning by making a generalization bound the objective to optimize. Direct optimization can nevertheless be computationally difficult, especially when repeatedly evaluating empirical risk is expensive. This paper develops an iterative alternative that uses a sequence of more tractable surrogate objectives derived from those bounds.

The key construction treats empirical risk as a function over hypotheses and projects it into a low-dimensional space of functions that can be constructed explicitly. The resulting projection can be queried much more cheaply than the original risk. The authors provide theoretical results establishing that iterative optimization of their surrogates implies optimization of the original generalization bounds.

They also apply the strategy to meta-learning, introducing an objective whose meta-gradient has a closed-form expression. Numerical experiments inspired by an industrial biochemical problem illustrate the approach. The contribution combines a general recipe, a theoretical connection to the original objective, and a concrete learning application, showing how cheaper intermediate calculations can retain a principled relationship to generalization-bound optimization.
neurips-2024-learning-via-surrogate-pac-.tldr: Surrogate PAC-Bayes replaces expensive risk evaluations with low-dimensional approximations while retaining a theoretical link to optimizing the original generalization bounds.

paragraphs: LRM-Zero investigates whether a model can learn to reconstruct real objects in three dimensions using training data made entirely by procedural synthesis. Its training collection, Zeroverse, starts from simple geometric primitives and adds random textures and transformations such as height fields, boolean differences, and wireframes. No realistic overall object meaning is built into the dataset.

Instead, Zeroverse emphasizes complicated local geometry and texture. Those details can resemble local features of real objects or be even more intricate, although the complete synthetic shapes need not resemble meaningful objects. This separates the availability of rich local reconstruction cues from the presence of realistic global object semantics in the training collection.

The resulting model produces high-quality sparse-view reconstructions of real objects, with visual quality competitive with models trained on Objaverse. The authors also analyze dataset design decisions that affect reconstruction capability and training stability. Their findings suggest that realistic object semantics may not be required to address this reconstruction task, demonstrating a potential role for fully synthesized training data.
neurips-2024-lrm-zero-training-large-rec.tldr: LRM-Zero learns competitive real-object 3D reconstruction from entirely synthetic shapes rich in local detail but lacking realistic global semantics.

paragraphs: Language models that handle standard queries well can still struggle with advanced mathematics requiring many connected reasoning steps. The paper identifies two issues with existing prompting approaches: limited effectiveness on difficult problems and dependence on prompts designed for individual problems. Both make it harder to apply a reasoning method across varied mathematical settings.

MACM introduces a multi-agent prompting system organized around condition mining. The approach makes identifying useful mathematical conditions a central part of the proposed reasoning method. The authors present it as a way to solve intricate problems while generalizing across mathematical contexts, addressing the need for a prompting method that can be reused beyond individual questions.

The reported result is an increase in GPT-4 Turbo accuracy from 54.68% to 76.73% on level-five problems in the MATH dataset, its most challenging level. This provides concrete evidence of improved performance in the evaluated setting. The contribution concerns how an existing language model is prompted and organized for difficult reasoning, with condition mining as the defining focus.
neurips-2024-macm-utilizing-a-multi-agen.tldr: MACM uses multi-agent condition mining to improve mathematical reasoning, raising GPT-4 Turbo accuracy on MATH level-five problems from 54.68% to 76.73%.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-experts layers divide computation among smaller components that can specialize. Increasing the number of experts could make their roles more specific, but the computational cost becomes a barrier. This paper introduces the Multilinear Mixture of Experts layer, or μMoE, to make fine-grained specialization more scalable, with a primary focus on vision models.

The layer computes implicitly with a very large weight tensor while keeping the computation entirely factorized. This avoids the high inference cost of dense expert mixtures and the training issues associated with discrete, non-differentiable routing in popular sparse mixtures. Factorization is the mechanism that makes the otherwise prohibitively large expert structure manageable.

When fine-tuning vision foundation models, qualitative and quantitative results show that scaling these layers produces stronger class-level specialization. The authors also demonstrate manual bias correction in CelebA attribute classification. In separate pretraining experiments, parameter-matched μMoE blocks throughout GPT2 and MLP-Mixer models retain comparable accuracy while displaying qualitative expert specialization. These findings connect scalable expert structure with opportunities to inspect and edit model behavior.
neurips-2024-multilinear-mixture-of-expe.tldr: Multilinear expert layers use factorized computation to scale specialization efficiently, with evidence of class-specific experts and manual bias correction.

paragraphs: Predictive coding updates a network's internal activities through iterative inference before changing its weights. This procedure can reduce the number of learning steps compared with backpropagation, but that advantage is not consistently observed. The paper investigates the geometry of the weight objective after the internal activities have reached inference equilibrium.

For deep linear networks, the authors show that the equilibrated energy equals mean squared error multiplied by a weight-dependent scaling factor. They then prove that many degenerate saddle points, including the origin, become strict saddles in this energy. Such points have a direction of negative curvature, making escape easier than at the corresponding highly degenerate saddles.

Experiments with linear and nonlinear networks support the theory and suggest that every saddle of the equilibrated energy might be strict. That broader statement remains an experimental suggestion in the abstract, beyond the proved result for many saddles. The work links predictive-coding inference to a more favorable landscape and greater robustness to vanishing gradients, while also identifying scaling to very deep networks as a fundamental challenge.
neurips-2024-only-strict-saddles-in-the-.tldr: Predictive-coding inference provably makes many saddles easier to escape in deep linear networks, with experiments suggesting a broader effect.

paragraphs: The paper examines what happens when a deep neural network perfectly classifies training examples even though their labels contain noise. Perfect fitting includes fitting that noise, so the central question is how this affects behavior beyond the training set. The analysis concerns fully connected networks whose weights are binary.

The authors consider two ways to choose a network that fits every training example. One selects a network with the smallest possible number of weights; the other selects a random interpolating network. For both rules, they prove tempered overfitting, establishing a controlled form of overfitting despite exact agreement with noisy training labels.

The proof relies on a new bound on the size of a threshold circuit consistent with a partial function. This supplies the mathematical foundation for analyzing both selection rules. According to the authors, these are the first theoretical results on benign or tempered overfitting that apply to deep networks without requiring extremely high or extremely low input dimension. The conclusions concern the specified binary-weight networks and learning rules.
neurips-2024-provable-tempered-overfitti.tldr: The paper proves tempered overfitting for minimal and randomly selected binary-weight deep networks that perfectly fit noisy training data.

paragraphs: This paper evaluates machine-learning dataset development using principles from data curation, a field rooted in libraries and archives. The authors develop a documentation rubric and toolkit from a literature review, then apply them systematically to 60 datasets published in the NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks track between 2021 and 2023.

The assessment identifies strengths and weaknesses in how datasets are documented. Its findings point to a greater need for information about environmental footprint, ethical considerations, and data management. These are documentation findings: they identify areas where descriptions need improvement and where clearer records could support more informed assessment and reuse.

The authors propose targeted resources and strategies for those areas, recommendations for the NeurIPS review process, and guidance for developers using the rubric independently. They also release their assessment results as a dataset intended to demonstrate aspects of recommended curation practice. The work provides both an evaluation of current practices and a reusable tool for improving documentation, with the aim of strengthening reproducibility, reusability, and human oversight.
neurips-2024-the-state-of-data-curation-.tldr: An assessment of 60 NeurIPS datasets identifies documentation gaps and offers a reusable rubric for improving data curation.

paragraphs: The Segment Anything Model can generalize widely, yet it often struggles with intricate image structures. Fine-tuning on carefully annotated examples can improve those cases. The authors show empirically, however, that this can also reduce performance on segmentation tasks absent from the fine-tuning data, weakening the model's original breadth.

Their Segmentation with Uncertainty Model, or SUM, combines high-quality annotations with a large unlabeled dataset. It quantifies uncertainty in the labels that SAM generates for those unlabeled images and uses that information during fine-tuning. A task prompt also identifies the kind of segmentation associated with each example, reducing ambiguity in what the model is being asked to segment.

The framework achieves state-of-the-art results across a test collection of 14 public benchmarks. Across point-prompt interactive segmentation rounds, it exceeds SAM by 3–6 points in mean intersection over union and 4–7 points in the boundary version of that metric. These results support combining uncertainty-aware learning and explicit task information when improving segmentation quality while seeking to preserve generalization.
neurips-2024-uncertainty-aware-fine-tuni.tldr: SUM combines uncertainty-aware learning from unlabeled images with task prompts to improve SAM segmentation while addressing fine-tuning-induced forgetting.

paragraphs: Discussions of emergent language-model abilities often focus on model size or training compute. This paper instead examines pretraining loss as the organizing variable. The motivation is that smaller models can sometimes perform well on supposedly emergent tasks, while discontinuous evaluation metrics have raised questions about whether observed jumps reflect the abilities themselves.

The authors find that Transformers reaching the same pretraining loss achieve the same performance on various downstream tasks despite differences in model and training-data size. This comparison holds with the data corpus, tokenization, and model architecture fixed. Those conditions matter because they define the setting in which loss aligns downstream performance across different scales.

For certain tasks, performance remains at random-guessing level until loss crosses a particular threshold, after which the ability appears. The authors observe this regardless of whether the evaluation metric is continuous. They therefore propose defining emergence through lower pretraining loss: performance after the threshold cannot be predicted merely by extending trends seen among models with higher loss.
neurips-2024-understanding-emergent-abil.tldr: Under fixed training conventions, pretraining loss aligns downstream performance across model scales and reveals thresholds for certain emergent abilities.

paragraphs: This paper introduces transformer backdoors designed to resist attempts by defenders to trigger them during evaluation. The construction uses cryptographic techniques to make the malicious behavior unelicitable, even when defenders have full access to the model's internal structure. This challenges evaluation strategies that depend on producing examples of dangerous behavior before deployment.

The authors distinguish this inability to trigger a backdoor from complete inability to detect its presence. Their universal backdoors are not completely undetectable under white-box access, although they can be harder to detect than some previous designs. That distinction matters: finding evidence that a model contains a backdoor and successfully eliciting its behavior are separate evaluation problems.

Empirical investigations confirm robustness properties of the construction and provide evidence that the backdoors can withstand state-of-the-art mitigation strategies. The authors also demonstrate their integration into transformer models. The findings question how much assurance predeployment red-teaming and certain formal verification methods can provide against this class of attack, while preserving the distinction between unelicitability and undetectability.
neurips-2024-unelicitable-backdoors-via-.tldr: Cryptographic transformer backdoors can resist triggering during white-box evaluation and withstand tested mitigations without being completely undetectable.

paragraphs: WelQrate addresses the quality of evaluation in small-molecule drug discovery. The authors argue that advances in models need a sound benchmarking framework to translate effectively into practical discovery. They introduce a collection of nine curated datasets spanning five therapeutic target classes, together with a standardized evaluation framework.

The curation process goes beyond the initial high-throughput screen by incorporating confirmatory screens, counter screens, and expert-designed preprocessing. This includes filtering Pan-Assay Interference Compounds. The evaluation framework also accounts for molecular featurization, three-dimensional conformation generation, metrics, and data splits, making these choices explicit parts of the benchmark rather than treating dataset selection as the whole evaluation problem.

The authors use WelQrate to investigate how models, dataset quality, feature representations, and splitting strategies affect reported performance. Their contribution is a coordinated dataset and evaluation resource intended to support real-world virtual screening. They recommend it as a gold standard and release the datasets, curation code, and experimental scripts, providing the materials needed to apply and examine the proposed benchmarking practices.
neurips-2024-welqrate-defining-the-gold-.tldr: WelQrate combines expert-curated molecular datasets with standardized evaluation practices to strengthen benchmarking for virtual screening.

paragraphs: Repeatedly updating a language model creates competing demands: edits should work reliably, generalize to relevant queries, and leave unrelated knowledge intact. The authors find that direct parameter editing and retrieval-based working memory struggle to achieve all three together in lifelong editing. Direct edits can conflict with existing knowledge, while retrieved representations can generalize poorly.

WISE introduces two parametric memories: a main memory holding pretrained knowledge and a side memory holding edits. Only the side memory is edited, and a trained router chooses which memory a query should use. This makes the placement of updated knowledge and the decision to access it explicit parts of the system.

For continual updates, WISE places different groups of edits in distinct parameter subspaces and subsequently merges them into a shared memory without conflicts. Experiments across question answering, hallucination, and out-of-distribution settings report improvements over previous editing methods on GPT, LLaMA, and Mistral architectures. These results support the authors' claim that WISE overcomes the observed three-way tradeoff in their evaluated lifelong-editing settings.
neurips-2024-wise-rethinking-the-knowled.tldr: WISE separates pretrained and edited knowledge into routed parametric memories to improve reliability, generalization, and locality during continual model editing.
